messages:
ravi: kicking off magellan-13b bring-up on dedicated infra, seeing some strange kv-cache divergences when seq_len > 4096. logged a small repro. anyone seen this pattern?
jen: can you paste the failing log lines? rough symptoms?
ravi: sure: 
```
kv_cache.shape: (12, 512, 64)
kv_store_count: 512
kv_read_count: 511
warning: kv index mismatch at layer 8 pos 4096
```
seems like one slot is dropped intermittently when using chunked attention + q8 quant.
chris: hmmm, sounds like an off-by-one in the index arithmetic when we splice chunks for rope positions. seen similar with rotary wrapping once. what runtime + kernel combo?
ravi: runtime=redwood-runtime v1.9.2, kernel opt set=auto, device=ampere-p4d (cuda 12), quant=q8fast. this only reproduces on GPU, CPU baseline is fine.
adele: GPU-only points to a kernel-level vectorization assumption. also check if the rotary angle computation is done in fp16 vs fp32 — fp16 phase accumulation can wrap early and cause position collisions.
lukas: confirmed: angles computed with fp16 in our fused attention kernel. hf reference uses fp32 for angle table then casts. that could shift cos/sin at high positions.
megan: could also be data layout: our kv_pack() pads to 512 but chunk boundary code uses < instead of <= in one place. quick grep shows `for i in range(0, n_packed-1)` in attention_chunker.
jen: ok two suspects: fp16 rotary table vs off-by-one in chunk loop. which is easiest to instrument?
chris: I'll add asserts in kernel harness to dump kv indices for the failing layer and compare with CPU run. small patch: add `CHECK(kv_read_count == kv_store_count)` in debug build.
ci-bot: CI job queued: infra/kv-harness/1976543210-debug-run (queued) :gear:
ravi: repro command for whoever wants to run locally: 
```
python -m tests.repro_magellan --model magellan-13b --seq 8196 --quant q8fast --device cuda --dump-kv debug/kvdump.json
```
(note seq 8196 to hit boundary)
adele: for mitigation, can we compute rotary angles in fp32 and cast later, or maintain angle table in host memory and read as fp32?
lukas: cheap patch: compute angles as fp32 in host table, store fp16 copy only for inference but use fp32 for index math in chunker. i'll try that + fix loop condition.
megan: also add a unit test that runs seq lengths around boundaries: 4095..4098 and checks kv consistency between CPU/GPU. will add to test/kv_regressions.py
jen: put a TODO in INF-1287 for telemetry to catch kv_read_count != kv_store_count in prod traces.
ravi: great. volunteer matrix: lukas will push kernel + angle patch, chris will run harness and capture kvdumps, megan will add unit/regression tests, jen will add infra alert. i'll follow up with a minimal bisect to confirm which change fixed it.
chris: one more note — observed tiny logit diffs (~1e-3) even after kv fix for q8fast; might be quant noise not bug. keep an eye on quality evals. :thinking_face:
jen: noted. add to nightly evals: magellan-13b/long-context/regression.
ravi: thanks folks. tagging @adele for follow-up on float precision docs.
adele: on it. will write short doc blurb outlining rotary fp precision assumptions + chunking caveats. :memo:
megan: PRs incoming. will link here when ready. :rocket:
